newsitem.title: UK: ATHLETICS-LONDON MARATHON HAUNTED BY FEARS OF IRA ACTION.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-LONDON MARATHON HAUNTED BY FEARS OF IRA ACTION.

text.p: Runners and spectators at Sunday's London Marathon have been warned to be vigilant against possible IRA activity which could ruin another of Britain's biggest sporting events.

Hoax bomb warnings by the Irish Republican Army (IRA) forced the Grand National steeplechase to be abandoned less than an hour before the start last week, raising fears that the marathon could be the next event on the guerrillas' hitlist.
More than 500,000 spectators are expected to watch the 27,000 runners along the 26 mile route through central London, making it one of the most difficult sporting events to protect.
"There will be high levels of vigilance. We always take the security of runners and the event very seriously," a spokeswoman for the London Marathon said on Saturday.
London police declined to comment on security arrangements but said that "every contingency" had been catered for.
"We always ask everyone to be vigilant," a police spokeswoman said.
"As with any major public event held in London, police work closely with organisers to ensure that the appropriate security measures are in place," the spokeswoman added.
The IRA, which is seeking an end to British rule of Northern Ireland, has stepped up activity to coincide with the campaign for the May 1 general election.
The bomb hoaxes which disrupted the Grand National followed a campaign of real and false bomb warnings which have caused chaos on British motorways and railways in the past three weeks.

Nothern Ireland peace talks, from which the IRA's political wing has been been excluded, have been suspended during the British election campaign but had been bogged down over procedural difficulties for months.
